source: bot-run (key screenshots only; no play.json yet)

profile.onboarding: Home screen shows 3 large picture-labeled buttons (Playground, Race, My Balls) with no tutorial text or spoken instructions. Reaching play requires a setup screen first: Race has 5 level cards plus race-length chips and a Go button; Playground has roughly 18 option buttons plus Go. Exact taps-to-play not measured.
profile.controls: Not shown directly in any screenshot — no on-screen control hints/overlay appear during play, only a persistent 'Home (hold)' button. Specific input method (touch-drag, tilt, etc.) not measured.
profile.core_loop: Roll the ball forward along a track, steering through curves, ramps, gaps, and hazards to reach the finish gate, repeating across 5 race levels or Playground/Race heats.
profile.goals_and_rewards: Crossing the finish triggers a 'FINISH' banner, checkmark, and confetti burst (winning-test-track-finish.png); in Race mode a live '1st' placement badge appears at finish and a podium results screen with a gold medal follows (winning-race-results.png). Source strings also reference unlockable skins/new balls (e.g. 'New ball!') though not directly observed in these shots.
profile.difficulty_curve: Five race levels escalate from 'Rolling Hills' to 'Going Big'/'Hammer Time', adding hazards like swinging hammers and wrecking balls per source, and Playground lets a grown-up dial up terrain and feature density. Fail cost is low: falling through a track gap simply respawns the ball at the last checkpoint with no penalty message (failing-gap-fall.png, failing-respawn.png).
profile.game_feel: Not measured — no fps or responsiveness data from a bot run. Screenshots show a smooth-looking low-poly 3D ball and a celebratory confetti burst on finish, suggesting positive feedback on success.
profile.art_and_audio: Bright, flat-shaded low-poly 3D style with bold black-outlined text and high-contrast buttons. Per source analysis there are 0 bundled audio files and no speechSynthesis use — only WebAudio sound effects, no music or voice-over.
profile.session_length: Not measured — no bot play data (play.json) available for time-to-first-win, retries, or session duration.
profile.usability: Home screen is clean (3 buttons + gear icon), but Playground setup crams about 18-19 simultaneous buttons/panels (size, surface, terrain, 5 features, star density, world code, Go, Back) and Race setup shows 5 track cards plus 4 race-length chips at once — both exceed comfortable button counts for either age bracket. During play, fail, and win screens, only a 'Home (hold)' control is visible, with no visible pause or mute icon.
profile.accessibility: Text uses bold outlines or white-on-saturated-color styling throughout for contrast, and selected setup options are marked with a thicker border rather than color alone (contrast checks pass for both brackets). However, the Sound toggle lives in Settings behind the 'Grown-ups (hold)' gate on Home, so it's unclear a child can mute audio mid-game without an adult — flagged as unsure/needs human review.
profile.ads_and_purchases: None seen in any screenshot or extracted game text.
profile.notes: Race mode adds a 3-2-1-GO countdown and simultaneous opponents with live placement — flagged as mild time-pressure for the 5-7 bracket (softened by being an optional mode) but acceptable for 8-10. No spoken/narrated instructions exist anywhere (confirmed by source: no speechSynthesis, no voice audio), a gap for early readers in the 5-7 bracket facing labels like 'Level 2: Bumpy Road'. Overall content-check result was NEEDS_HUMAN, pending confirmation of in-play mute access.
